subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core memory trust-policy model, and should this issue remain the canonical tracker for source trust tiers and retrieval policy after the narrower provenance work lands?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the correct boundary spans security policy, persisted memory schema, plugin/SDK contracts, retrieval ranking, config surface, and UI/docs, so automation cannot choose the product direction safely.

options.title: Keep This As Trust-Policy Canonical
options.body: Use this issue for source trust tiers, review/expiration policy, and trust-aware retrieval while linking provenance and autoCapture items as prerequisites or narrower slices.

options.title: Split Under Provenance MVP
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42647 the canonical data-model prerequisite and keep this issue only for retrieval policy after provenance lands.

options.title: Endorse Plugin/MCP Path Only
options.body: Treat world-model-mcp and similar integrations as the path for advanced trust scoring unless a missing OpenClaw memory/plugin API is proven.

recommendation.title: Keep This As Trust-Policy Canonical
recommendation.body: Use this issue for source trust tiers, review/expiration policy, and trust-aware retrieval while linking provenance and autoCapture items as prerequisites or narrower slices.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current memory contract blame signal and already provided the prior review framing for this exact issue.
